page.layout: One heading line in italics across the top, then one table: a column of years on the left (with small marks above some years), and a column of names to the right, cut off at the right edge of the scan. Horizontal rules divide the years into groups.; One column of short line-ends at the right edge of a page, below a running head at the top; horizontal rules divide the lines into groups.; Page number 291 at top right. Left of the page: a ruled table, cut off at the left edge, with a cell reading "Coppen" and "(Iarges." Below the table, the catchword "Iohan". Right margin: one column of marginal notes marked *, † and ‡, running from top to bottom.

marginalia.note: * Diploma Cæsaris luculentissimum pro Groninganis a Loe allatum, signatum anno priore: quo munus gubernationis per Frisiam Occidentalem ijs commissum.

‡ Pactum civitatis cum Monasteriensibus de derivan-do Amasio.
Obiit Heydelberge die 28. Oct. Rudolphus Agricola, postquam annos vixisset XLII. menses 2.
Ius cudendæ Monetæ Aureæ civitas ti Groning. datum ab Imp. Friderico III.

page.notes: Years are printed in old-style figures in a column beside the names. Marks *, †, and ‡ stand above the years 1481, 1482 and 1483 and are kept in the table. The names are read only as far as the scan shows them; the right-hand ends of the lines are not visible. The heading reads only "Reip", with the rest not visible. Rules between the year groups are not text. Only the right-hand ends of the lines are legible; the word beginnings are not on this part. Reading of the running head is doubtful. The ruled table at the left is cut off, so only its right-hand cells are legible. "civitas ti" is printed across a line end; the join is uncertain, so check it against the original. The reference marks *, † and ‡ are copied from the notes; their places in the main text are not on this part of the scan.
